messages:
leila: hi team, i'm leila (new runtime eng). trying to build from source on ubuntu 22.04 with CUDA 12.2 but the link stage fails with nvrtc/ptx errors. not sure what to try next. any onboarding tips? :wave:

omar: welcome leila! can you paste the exact linker error? quick guesses: mixed CUDA installs, stray libcuda in /usr/lib, or host driver mismatch.

leila: paste of the end of the build log:
```
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libnvrtc-builtins.so: undefined reference to `__nvvm_demote_to_global'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[2]: *** [runtime/libinference.so] Error 1
```

leila: nvcc --version shows CUDA 12.2.148, nvidia-smi shows Driver 515.48.07 (CUDA 12.2).

sophia: welcome! that particular symbol often means there's a mix between toolkit components (libnvrtc vs nvvm) compiled for different CUDA micro versions. did you install CUDA via the .deb meta package or from distro packages? also any conda envs that bundle CUDA?

leila: i used the nvidia-runfile installer to put cuda-12.2 in /usr/local and then `apt install libcuda1` earlier for some deps. not in a conda env.

omar: two things to try: 1) check for duplicate CUDA libraries on the linker path: `ldconfig -p | grep nvrtc` and `readlink -f $(which nvcc)`. 2) inspect /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu for leftover nvrtc or nvvm libs that come from distro packages. If there are duplicates, remove the older ones or reorder LD_LIBRARY_PATH so /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 comes first.

leila: ldconfig output shows an nvrtc at /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvrtc.so.14 and also at /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libnvrtc.so.12.

sophia: aha — conflicting major versions. linker is probably picking the distro nvrtc (v14) while nvcc and the rest are v12. That causes the symbol mismatch. Best fix: remove the distro nvrtc package (`sudo apt purge nvidia-cuda-toolkit libnvrtc*`) or prefer the cuda-12.2 paths by exporting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before building and run `sudo ldconfig`. We also prefer dev containers for onboarding to avoid host contamination.

leila: i'm hesitant to purge system packages on my laptop. is there a safer local workaround?

omar: yeah you can set env for the build only: `export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64:/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/stubs:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and then `make clean && make -j8`. If the linker still picks the wrong lib, check `gcc -Wl,-verbose` to see lib search order. Alternatively, run the repo's docker image `ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rt-dev:cuda12.2` which isolates the toolchain.

leila: tried LD_LIBRARY_PATH trick, rebuild fails but now the symbol error changed to a missing `libnvvm` symbol. i think it's getting one but not the matching one.

sophia: if you're seeing successive missing nvvm/nvrtc symbols, that usually means multiple mismatched versions. For a non-invasive approach: install the *same* CUDA runtime libs under a local prefix and point LD_LIBRARY_PATH to that single prefix. Otherwise use the dev docker image. For laptop onboarding we have a script `scripts/onboard-quick.sh` which sets env and prints known conflicts. run that and paste the output.

leila: ran onboard-quick.sh, it flagged `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvvm.so.3` as coming from `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` and `/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libnvvm.so` from the toolkit runfile. flagged mismatch.

omar: two practical routes: 1) remove `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` (safe if you don't rely on distro CUDA packages) or 2) use the dev container or a VM image. For workstations we recommend driver 535+ with matching toolkit installs — older drivers like 515 can sometimes be OK but mixing distro toolkit versions leads to exactly this. If you must keep both, add an rpath to the target binary pointing to the correct /usr/local/cuda-12.2 lib dir.

infra-bot: Note: company image ghcr.io/redwood-inference/rt-dev:cuda12.2 is prebuilt with CUDA 12.2 and matching driver libs; recommended for new devs.

leila: ok i'll try the docker/dev image path for now. question: who maintains the onboarding script and the known-good driver/toolkit matrix? i couldn't find a clear owner.

sophia: runtime infra owns it (cc @omar). we should add a small table to docs/runtime/runtime-setup.md listing driver and toolkit combos we've verified. feel free to open a docs PR; i'll review.

ci-bot: CI Check: branch leila/onboard-nvrtc - pre-submit lint passed, build not executed (requires NVIDIA host).

leila: thanks all, switching to the dev image to continue. i'll open a PR to docs after i confirm which driver we used. appreciate the help! :pray:
